solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Group of bacteria producing nasty eye spot right inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the abbreviation for right sits within the jumbled letters
something nasty is in a bad way, so the letters of eye spot are jumbled

explanation.surface: A doctor describes a microbe colony that causes an unpleasant spot in the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges EYE SPOT, and 'inside' puts R within that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A serotype is a distinct variety within a bacterial species, classified by its surface antigens, so it is a group of bacteria.

clue.text: Box missing a tool in lounge

indicators.note: missing tells us the letter a is dropped from the box word

parts.note: to spar is to box in practice
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.surface: A boxing session without a piece of kit, held in the lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes A from SPAR, leaving SPR. 'lounge' looks like a room but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprawl is to sit or lie with limbs spread out lazily, a way of lolling about.

clue.text: Second-hand dealer managed to hold meeting once a year

indicators.note: to hold means the managed word contains the meeting

parts.note: ran means managed, as one runs a business
AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: A trader in used goods organised a yearly company meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting once a year' is the British abbreviation for an annual general meeting of a company or club.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragman collects and sells old clothes and scraps, a trader in used goods.

clue.text: Student Union given little support

parts.note: TU is short for trade union
a tee is the small peg supporting a golf ball

explanation.surface: The Students' Union is given a small amount of backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Student Union' reads as one body, but Student is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a pupil being taught by a tutor.

clue.text: Get anything but a quack remedy?

parts.note: pro means a professional, the opposite of a quack or charlatan
a cure is a remedy for illness

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks whether one can obtain any treatment that is not fake medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure something is to obtain it, often with effort.

clue.text: Protests about one heavenly body

indicators.note: about means the protests word goes round the letter for one

parts.note: demos is short for demonstrations, public protests
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Demonstrators are angry about a particular star or planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places DEMOS round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Deimos is the smaller of the two moons of Mars, a natural satellite and so a celestial object.

clue.text: Alluring woman's let go to ensnare a spy

indicators.note: to ensnare means the woman's words trap the letter inside

parts.note: Eve, the temptress of Genesis, in the possessive form
to drop is to let go of something

explanation.surface: A seductress drops her guard to trap a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alluring woman' points to Eve, the temptress of Genesis; 'spy' looks like a noun but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly to others' conversation, a kind of covert snooping.

clue.text: Insect making beastly noise — son has to clear off inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the son and clear-off letters go within the noise

parts.note: a moo is the sound cattle make
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to quit is to leave or clear off

explanation.surface: A buzzing bug makes a racket, and a boy has to get rid of it indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosquito is a small biting fly, a well-known pest among flying bugs.

clue.text: Platform needs unendingly reliable flock surrounding leader of Conservatives

indicators.note: surrounding means the letters wrap round the Tory leader's initial
unendingly means the final letter of the reliable word is cut

parts.note: safe means dependable or reliable

indicators.note: leader of points to the first letter of the party name

parts.note: a fold is a flock of sheep, or the pen holding them

explanation.surface: A political stage needs a loyal congregation around the Tory leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unendingly' drops the final E; the party initial goes in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised wooden platform, historically used for public executions.

clue.text: Time to beat the bounds? You want rain to go somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of rain to go get arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone planning a walk round the parish boundary hopes the rain will clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges RAIN TO GO. Beating the bounds is an old English parish custom of walking its boundary and striking landmarks with sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogation days, before Ascension Day, were the traditional season for parishioners to walk and mark their parish boundaries.

clue.text: One version of Bible established a number of religious texts

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible
EST is the standard abbreviation for established, as on shop signs

explanation.surface: A particular Bible translation set up a collection of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avesta is the collection of sacred scriptures of Zoroastrianism, a body of several religious works.

clue.text: Hit wicket — clumsy!

parts.note: W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
ham, as in ham-fisted, means clumsy or inept

explanation.surface: A cricket batter knocks over their own stumps, a dismissal called hit wicket, and is mocked for clumsiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit wicket' looks like one cricket phrase, but Hit is the definition and wicket gives W.
explanation.definitionFit: A wham is a heavy, resounding blow, so it serves as a noun for a hit or strike.

clue.text: Dreadful horsemeat fraud news causes mad fear — it's a brief unreal experience for us!

definitions.text: it's a brief unreal experience for us

indicators.note: dreadful implies the words are in a terrible state, so their letters get rearranged

parts.words: horsemeat fraud news causes mad fear

explanation.surface: A headline about the horsemeat scandal says the news is spreading panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges all 31 letters of the fodder. The answer is Prospero's line in Shakespeare's The Tempest, which goes on 'and our little life is rounded with a sleep'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation says human life is made of dream-stuff, a fleeting and illusory thing, which the clue paraphrases.

clue.text: See 12
Request not to permit drug that's a poison

parts.note: to ban is to order that something is not allowed
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Someone asks that a toxic drug be prohibited.
explanation.definitionFit: Bane is an old word for poison, surviving in plant names such as wolfsbane.

clue.text: See 12
Marriage's warlike with couple inside rolling round

definitions.note: a possessive acting as an adjective, of or belonging to marriage

indicators.note: rolling round means the inner pair of letters turn the other way

parts.note: martial means warlike, to do with fighting
the two letters in the middle of the warlike word

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that wedlock is a battle with the pair wrestling inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling round' turns the two middle letters of the warlike word the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital is the adjective for things belonging to wedlock, matching the possessive form.

clue.text: Mob wanting British out in endless disturbance — they never get worn out

indicators.note: in means the reduced mob goes inside the shortened disturbance
endless means the last letter of the disturbance word is dropped

parts.note: a dust or dust-up is a row or commotion

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter for British is taken away

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly mob

explanation.surface: A crowd without the Brits is caught up in an ongoing commotion, tireless people indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting British out' drops one B; 'endless' cuts the final letter, and 'in' puts the reduced mob inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Durables are long-lasting consumer goods, such as fridges, that are made to resist wear.

clue.text: In gym I flounder, with refusal to be held in dishonour

indicators.note: to be held means the refusal sits inside the jumbled letters
to flounder is to struggle clumsily, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A gym-goer struggles and, being turned down, feels shamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounder' rearranges the first three words to IGMINY, and 'to be held' puts the refusal inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignominy is public shame and disgrace.

clue.text: A foreign fellow hanging around university is a greasy type

parts.note: un is the French word for a

indicators.note: hanging around means the fellow word surrounds the university letter

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: An oily foreign man loiters near a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging around' puts U inside GENT. 'greasy type' sounds like an unsavoury man but means a kind of ointment.
explanation.definitionFit: An unguent is a soothing ointment or salve, an oily preparation for the skin.

clue.text: Silent leader has left work

indicators.note: the leading letter of the silent word departs

parts.note: still means quiet or silent

explanation.surface: A quiet boss has gone to their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader has left' drops the S from STILL.
explanation.definitionFit: To till is to cultivate the soil, working the land by ploughing.

clue.text: Church member needing to suffer a punishment I ignored

indicators.note: ignored tells us the letter I is left out of the phrase

parts.note: cop it is British slang for getting into trouble or being punished

explanation.surface: A churchgoer must face a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes I from COP IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Copt belongs to the Coptic Orthodox Church of Egypt, so is a member of a Christian denomination.

clue.text: Daughter leaving country, grabbing good man? It's a game!

indicators.note: grabbing means the shortened country takes hold of the good man
leaving means the daughter letter goes out of the country

parts.note: Canada is the North American country
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
ST stands for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A girl emigrates, taking a decent fellow with her, and treats it all as play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes D from CANADA, giving CANAA, which then goes 'grabbing' ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-type card game played with two packs.

clue.text: Inane holiday worker

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a holiday
an ant is the classic crossword worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A seasonal employee is dismissed as dim-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant means blank and showing no intelligence, as in a vacant stare, so empty-headed.

clue.text: Maybe audibly ban smoker in church

indicators.note: audibly means we take a word that sounds the same as the banning one

parts.note: to censor something, such as a book, is to suppress or ban it

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone should forbid smoking in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks censoring as one kind of banning.
explanation.definitionFit: A censer is a vessel for burning incense, swung during services so it gives off smoke.

clue.text: Arab ruler carrying gold in old marketplace

indicators.note: carrying means the ruler holds the gold inside

parts.note: an aga is a title for a commander or chief in the Ottoman world
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A ruler bearing gold through an ancient market.
explanation.walkthrough: An aga was strictly an Ottoman Turkish title, loosely called Arab here.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the open public square and market in ancient Greek cities.

clue.text: All needs worked out with English getting wartime help from USA

indicators.note: worked out means the letters of all needs are reorganised

explanation.surface: Britain's needs are calculated and met with American assistance during a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges ALL NEEDS to give LENDLEAS, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Lend-Lease was the 1941 American programme supplying arms and goods to Britain and other allies in the Second World War.

clue.text: Bird submerged under lake or swamp

indicators.note: in a down answer, submerged under means the bird is placed below the lake letter

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
the erne is the white-tailed sea eagle

explanation.surface: A bird dives beneath the water of a lake or marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: Lerna was the marsh near Argos where Hercules killed the Hydra.
explanation.definitionFit: Lerne, or Lerna, is the legendary marshland in Greek myth, the swamp home of the Hydra.

clue.text: Hard worker has time left to switch places and lurk

indicators.note: the letter for time and the letter for left exchange their positions in the worker word

parts.note: a toiler is someone who labours hard

explanation.surface: A diligent employee suddenly drifts off and hangs about.
explanation.walkthrough: In TOILER, T (time) and L (left) 'switch places', giving LOITER.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger about aimlessly, often with suspicion attached, close in sense to skulking.

clue.text: See 12
Old port? Gosh, our navy has docked in it!

indicators.note: has docked in means the navy's letters are lodged within the other word

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, SA
my is an exclamation of surprise like gosh
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's navy

explanation.surface: An exclamation as the British fleet berths in an ancient harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has docked in' puts MY and RN inside SA, the old crossword abbreviation for sex appeal, also called 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Smyrna was the ancient Aegean seaport now known as Izmir in Turkey.

clue.text: The old woman embracing individual, exuding love, a dominatrix?

indicators.note: embracing means the mother word wraps round what follows

parts.note: mater is old-fashioned slang for one's mother

indicators.note: exuding means the zero letter seeps out of the individual word

parts.note: one means a single individual
love is zero in tennis scoring, giving O

explanation.surface: Mother hugs someone, without affection, perhaps a domineering lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exuding' drops the love letter, leaving NE, and 'embracing' wraps the mother word round it with A.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is a woman who dominates and devours lovers, which the question mark admits a dominatrix may exemplify.
